item.title: “Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a…
item.description:
“Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a hiding place near the bait cast by Māra and the world’s offerings. Having made a hiding place, without entering, without indulging, we will eat the bait and the world’s offerings. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become infatuated; not infatuated, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not become subject to Māra’s will among that bait and offerings.’ These ascetics and brahmins make a hiding place near the bait and offerings. Having done so, without entering, without indulging, they eat the bait and offerings. Not entering, not indulging, they do not become infatuated; not infatuated, they do not become heedless; not heedless, they do not become subject to Māra’s will. But then they have such wrong views as: ‘The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite …’ Thus, monks, these third ascetics and brahmins have not escaped Māra’s power.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 25 – Nivāpasutta

item.title: “Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness…
item.description:
“Ānanda, those noble thoughts that are conducive to progress and lead to the complete destruction of suffering — such as renunciation thoughts, non-ill-will thoughts, harmlessness thoughts — he reflects: ‘I will think these thoughts.’ In this way, he is clearly aware of that.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 122 – Mahāsuññatasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will, monks … sloth and torpor … restlessness and…
item.description:
“Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will, monks … sloth and torpor … restlessness and remorse … doubt is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. These, monks, are the five obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.51
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is…
item.description:
“And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is perception? There are various perceptions, many and diverse: sensual perception, ill-will perception, harmfulness perception. From these, unwholesome thoughts arise.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 78 – Samaṇamuṇḍikasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense-bases cease … such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.39
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And what, Mahānāma, is the gratification of sensual pleasures? Mahānāma, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure: forms cognizable by the eye – desirable,…
item.description:
“And what, Mahānāma, is the gratification of sensual pleasures? Mahānāma, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure: forms cognizable by the eye – desirable, pleasurable, agreeable, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tangibles cognizable by the body – desirable, pleasurable, agreeable, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, Mahānāma, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on these five strands of sensual pleasure – that is the gratification of sensual pleasures.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 14 – Cūḷadukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nisabha: Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Those things so agreeable, Which delight the mind — With faith, I went forth, Putting…
item.description:
Elder Nisabha:

Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Those things so agreeable,
Which delight the mind —
With faith, I went forth,
Putting an end to suffering.

I do not delight in death,
I do not delight in life.
I await the time,
Mindful and clearly comprehending.

From: Theragāthā 2.38
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And what, monks, are the things that should be fully understood? Form, monks, is a thing that should be fully understood; feeling … perception ……
item.description:
“And what, monks, are the things that should be fully understood? Form, monks, is a thing that should be fully understood; feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is a thing that should be fully understood. These, monks, are the things that should be fully understood. And what, monks, is full understanding? The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion — this, monks, is called full understanding.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.23
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms. Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s body thrown in the charnel ground, just a skeleton…
item.description:
“Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms. Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s body thrown in the charnel ground, just a skeleton with white bones like a shell … bones more than a year old … rotting bones reduced to powder. What do you think, monks? Has the former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?”
“Yes, venerable sir.”
“Monks, such is the peril in the case of forms.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Householder, suppose a man carries a blazing grass torch against the wind. What do you think, householder? If that man does not quickly let go…
item.description:
“Householder, suppose a man carries a blazing grass torch against the wind. What do you think, householder? If that man does not quickly let go of that blazing torch, could it burn his hand, his arm, or some part of his body, and would he thereby meet death or deadly suffering?” “Yes, venerable sir.” … “So too, householder, a noble disciple reflects: ‘The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are like a grass torch — of much suffering, much despair, and the peril is even greater.’ Having seen this as it actually is with perfect wisdom … he cultivates such equanimity.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 54 – Potaliyasutta
